Grace (Finance): Heads up everyone  we've completed the annual expense policy review and are rolling out a couple of targeted changes starting Mon Aug 1. Short summary: new pre-approval thresholds for events and cloud prepayments, tightened recurring SaaS registration, and a new CFO sign-off for multi-year vendor commitments > $60k. Full memo: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/FIN/pages/Annual+Expense+Policy+2026 :memo:

Omar (Eng Ops): Can you list the main numeric thresholds quickly so teams know?

Grace (Finance): Sure  key bits: 1) Event/sponsorships >= $8k require centralized review + ROI doc. 2) Cloud credits or prepaid commitments > $40k require budget lock and Finance approval. 3) PCard single txn cap remains $5k but monthly aggregate per card capped at $8k (please avoid splitting). 4) Recurring SaaS must be registered in the SaaS inventory or finance will flag and require retro registration.

Priya (Product): For cloud prepayments, is the $40k threshold cumulative per vendor or per contract? We often prepay yearly for reserved capacity.

Grace (Finance): Per contract/commitment. If teams combine multiple services in one bundled prepayment and it's > $40k we treat as a single commitment. If you need an exception, submit the procurement ticket with project justification and tag "multi-year-exception".

Sasha (Accounting): Accounting notes: prepaid commitments > $40k should include expected invoice cadence and whether vendor invoices annually or upfront. For annual upfront invoices reference PO# and send to ap@redwood.com. GL for cloud services remains GL-4200.

Legal (Contracts): For multi-year deals > $60k, we require a standard review of automatic renewals and termination language. Please attach redlines early to avoid delays. CFO sign-off will be required before contract execution.

procure-bot: procurement ticket created: FIN-2026-4310 by Omar (Eng Ops)  status: awaiting intake.

Omar (Eng Ops): I filed FIN-2026-4310 for a 2-year reserved capacity commit ~ $72k. What is the expected review timeline?

Grace (Finance): For complete submissions: Finance intake 3 business days, Legal review 5-10 business days depending on redlines. CFO-level approvals add extra routing time; plan accordingly. If you need to accelerate for a launch, add [EXPEDITE] and include Eng manager + PM approvals in the ticket. Finance will triage same day.

Priya (Product): What counts as a "complete" submission? We had back-and-forth last quarter due to missing SOW.

Grace (Finance): Complete = vendor quote + SOW (if services), PO form filled with project_code & GL, vendor attestations (SOC2 if applicable), and billing instructions. We have a checklist on the memo page to copy into the ticket.

Sasha (Accounting): Side note on SaaS registration: any recurring subscription with single vendor spend > $12k/year must appear in the SaaS inventory before renewal. If it's missed, retroactive approval is harder. We'll reach out for remediations.

Omar (Eng Ops): If Legal requests contract changes that affect cost (eg penalties), does that revert to a new approval?

Legal (Contracts): If negotiated terms materially change financial exposure or renewal cadence, yes we re-run Finance approval. Flag changes in the ticket thread.

Grace (Finance): TL;DR: event >= $8k centralized review; cloud prepayments > $40k need budget lock; multi-year > $60k gets CFO sign-off; complete checklist required for 3-day intake. Policy page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/FIN/pages/Annual+Expense+Policy+2026 :white_check_mark:

Priya (Product): Thanks  will update our vendor intake template and tag FIN-2026-4310 with the SOW.

Sasha (Accounting): I'll update the PO template and SaaS inventory form today.

Omar (Eng Ops): Adding PM sign-off and SOW now. Thanks.
